# Responsive Plugin

> Other display/interaction plugins → grid-plugins-catalog-ui.md · plugin architecture → grid-plugins.md · CSS layers & animation vars → build-css.md.

## Overview

OWNS: breakpoint-based column visibility. HOOKS: afterRender, getRowHeight. Does NOT implement `processColumns` (the hook exists) — the column MODEL is never touched; `afterRender` toggles `data-responsive-hidden`/`-value-only` on `.cell[data-field]` **and** rewrites `--tbw-column-template` (`#applyColumnTemplate`, via `splitTrackList`/`collapsedTrack`) to collapse hidden tracks to `0px`.

- INVARIANT (Sep 2026, supersedes "hiding a column does NOT shrink the grid"): hiding a column now DOES shrink the grid. Core regenerates `--tbw-column-template` from the model every render, so `#applyColumnTemplate` must re-apply on every `afterRender` (`#templateOverridden` tracks a live override so it can be released). Verified at 1100/650/450px: trailing tracks go to `0px` and `scrollWidth === clientWidth` at every width (baseline was `750 / 427` with dead space).
- TRADE-OFF: a hidden NON-trailing column now makes later columns slide left (smoothly). Previously nothing shifted. This also fixes a latent bug — cells are purely auto-placed (no `grid-column` anywhere in core), so `display: none` on a mid-list column silently shifted every later cell into the wrong track; a collapsing cell must therefore stay in flow (zero-size box), never `display: none`.
- INVARIANT: the transition animating the track list is bound at ROW level (`tbw-grid[data-responsive-column-fade] :is(.header-row, .data-grid-row)`), not cell level. WHY: the header ROW element persists across renders while its CELLS are rebuilt (`header.ts` ~L160 `headerRow.innerHTML = ''`), so a cell-level transition restarts every render; the row-level one survives.
- INVARIANT: the collapse block's `opacity: 0` is deliberately NOT `!important` — `!important` outranks WAAPI animations and would kill the plugin-driven fade.

- INVARIANT: the header ROW is ALWAYS hidden in card mode (unconditional `tbw-grid[data-responsive] .header { display: none }`). `hideHeader` does NOT control that — it gates per-card FIELD LABELS (the `Name:` `::before` prefix).
- DECIDED (May 2026): `hideHeader` defaults to `false`; `#applyResponsiveState()` sets `data-responsive-hide-header` on the host only when `isResponsive && hideHeader === true` (CSS hides `.data-grid-row:not(.group-row) > .cell::before`), cleared on leaving card mode.
- DECIDED (Sep 2026): `debounceMs` is a **rate limit, not a delay**. `#onResize()` drops notifications where `width === #lastCheckedWidth`, switches on the LEADING edge when `performance.now() - #lastSwitchAt >= debounceMs`, else defers ONE trailing evaluation to `#lastSwitchAt + debounceMs`. WHY: `ResizeObserver` fires on HEIGHT too, and host apps animate container height (detail panel open/close) while the width is already final — the old `clearTimeout`+`setTimeout` per callback let ~15 height-only frames push the deadline out (measured equinor cost-allocation: width final at 10.6 ms, card mode at 363 ms → 6–13 ms after).
- INVARIANT: `#lastSwitchAt` MUST init to `Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY`, not `0`. `performance.now()` is 0 at page load (and under `vi.useFakeTimers()`), so `0` makes the very first evaluation take the deferred branch.
- FLOW (layout switch, Sep 2026): `#checkBreakpoint`/`#checkMultiBreakpoint`/`setResponsive` flip `#isResponsive` **synchronously** (so `isResponsive()` and `responsive-change` are immediate), then call `#commitLayoutSwitch()`, which defers the DOM change. With `Element.startViewTransition()` → sets `data-responsive-transition`, and in the update callback runs `#applyResponsiveState()` + `await grid.forceLayout()`. Without it → `#applyResponsiveState()` + `requestRender()` synchronously.
- DECIDED (Sep 2026): **element-scoped only** — `Element.startViewTransition()` (Chrome/Edge 147+), never `document.startViewTransition()`. Document-scoped is Baseline but render-suppresses the whole HOST page and its pseudo tree spills over clipping containers, so a grid would freeze the embedding app's own animations — precisely the detail-panel case that motivated this. Unsupported browsers keep the CSS keyframe fade.
- INVARIANT: `data-responsive-animate` and `data-responsive-transition` are **mutually exclusive** — `#applyResponsiveState()` withholds the former whenever `#supportsViewTransition`. WHY: `responsive-card-enter` is bound to `[data-responsive][data-responsive-animate]`, so suppressing it _during_ the transition only defers it — clearing `data-responsive-transition` restarts the keyframe and the card layout animates a second time. Symptom is asymmetric (enter flickers, exit is clean) because the keyframe only exists on `[data-responsive]`.
- INVARIANT: rAF **does** fire inside an element-scoped view transition's update callback (verified Chrome 151), which is what makes `await forceLayout()` — an rAF-batched render — usable there. Document-scoped transitions suppress the rendering steps and would deadlock until the 4 s timeout.
- DECIDED (Sep 2026): one `animation?: ResponsiveAnimation` (`false | 'fade' | 'morph-rows' | 'morph-cells'`, default `'fade'`) instead of three booleans — matches `ExpandCollapseAnimation`/`ReorderAnimation` across core+6 plugins, and makes the illegal rows+cells combination unrepresentable. `animate?: boolean` is DEPRECATED since 3.7.0 (kept: released API); `get #animation()` resolves it and is the SOLE reader — a direct `config.animate` read anywhere else silently ignores `animation`. Adapters only re-export the config type, so no adapter change was needed.
- DECIDED (Sep 2026): the morph styles author `view-transition-name` from `aria-rowindex` (+ `aria-colindex` for cells) with a per-instance prefix, set before the snapshot, re-applied after `forceLayout()`, cleared on `finished` and in `detach()`. Naming a row AND its cells lifts the cells out of the row's own snapshot, so cells win. `'morph-cells'` degrades to `'morph-rows'` above `MAX_MORPH_CELLS = 150`. NOT default: every named element is its own compositor layer. COST (measured Sep 2026, 36 cells → 108 animations): `3 × cells` animations (group+old+new) + `2 × cells` snapshot textures. Budget counts RENDERED cells, and rows are virtualized → bounded by viewport height × column count, not dataset size.
- INVARIANT (Sep 2026): a superseded view transition's `finished` cleanup MUST NOT tear down the names/attribute its successor captured — the UA then aborts the live one with `InvalidStateError`. `#transitionToken` is bumped per switch and `cleanup` returns early unless its token is still current. Reproduced by crossing the breakpoint every 120 ms against a 200 ms transition; a MutationObserver showed the add and the stale removal in the SAME millisecond. Also: `ViewTransition.ready` REJECTS whenever the UA skips a transition (routine during a resize drag), so it always needs a `.catch()` or it surfaces as an unhandled rejection.
- DECIDED (Sep 2026): names are AUTHORED, not `view-transition-name: match-element` — measured on the live docs page, cell node identity across a card↔table switch is **width-dependent**: 900→360 preserved 36/36 cells, 680→360 destroyed 36/36 on 3/3 runs (at 680 columns are already progressively hidden, so the switch also changes the rendered column set → `structureValid` false → `clearRowForRebuild` wipes `rowEl.innerHTML`). Rows survive either way. `match-element` would morph at some widths and silently cross-fade at others.
- INVARIANT: `view-transition-class` does NOT capture — MDN: "Each individual element still needs its own unique `view-transition-name`". It collapses N per-name rules into one `::view-transition-group(.tbw-responsive-cell)`; it saves CSS, never DOM writes. Duplicate names reject `ViewTransition.ready` and skip the transition.
- TRADE-OFF: card labels can't morph — they are `::before { content: attr(data-header) }` and `view-transition-name` is element-only; promoting them costs ~1 node per cell on the rows hot path, and it is 1:N (one header cell vs one label per row) while names are strictly 1:1.
- DECIDED (Sep 2026): a hidden-COLUMN change is excluded from the view transition — `#checkMultiBreakpoint` passes `layoutChanged` to `#commitLayoutSwitch`, which only calls `#viewTransitionStarter()` when the table/card layout actually flipped. WHY: nothing moves on a column change (track list unchanged), and the trigger is a resize DRAG, so the frozen whole-grid snapshot is scaled against a still-changing container — the reported "whole grid scales down and up".
- DECIDED (Sep 2026): the column fade is plugin-driven WAAPI (`#openFadeWindow`/`#playColumnFade`, tagged `Animation.id = 'tbw-responsive-column-fade'`), NOT a CSS transition. WHY: the header row is REBUILT every render (6 cells removed + 6 added; body cells ARE reused, header cells are NOT), so a re-inserted hidden cell is style-resolved visible and then transitions to hidden again — every already-hidden column flashes back in and re-fades. `#fadeEndsAt` lets a cell created mid-fade join in progress via `animation.currentTime`; a `setTimeout` closes the window and requests the final render, because a fading-out column withholds `data-responsive-hidden` (keeping its box, so neighbours never shift) until then.
- INVARIANT: `hiddenColumns` is INERT in a plain table — it applies only in card mode, or in progressive degradation when a breakpoint matches (`#hiddenColumnsApply`). So the fade is queued by diffing against `#appliedHiddenFields` (what the last `afterRender` actually hid), never against the previous CONFIG: queueing a fade-out for a column that stays visible strands it at `opacity: 0` in a track that is never collapsed (`fill: 'forwards'` holds it after the window closes). `#endFadeWindow()` therefore also CANCELS every lingering `tbw-responsive-column-fade`; past the window CSS owns visibility. `#commitLayoutSwitch` calls `#endFadeWindow()` on a real layout switch so fades never fight the view transition.
- INVARIANT (Sep 2026): `afterRender` must run its cell loop one more time AFTER the last field stops applying — body cells come from the recycled `_rowPool`, so `data-responsive-hidden`/`-value-only` written in card mode survive the switch back to table (columns stay invisible at `opacity: 0` in uncollapsed tracks). Guarded by `#appliedHiddenFields`/`#appliedValueOnlyFields` being non-empty; the early return only fires once the previous render applied nothing either.
- INVARIANT (#470): `detach()` MUST undo everything `#syncLayoutAttributes()` writes (`data-responsive`, `-animate`, `-hide-header`) plus `-transition` and the per-cell `data-responsive-hidden`/`-value-only`/`aria-hidden` markers. `tbw-grid[data-responsive-animate]` transitions `.data-grid-row`/`.cell` WITHOUT `[data-responsive]`, so a leftover keeps styling a grid the plugin no longer owns; leftover cell markers keep columns collapsed outright.
- INVARIANT (#470): `#commitLayoutSwitch()` is the SOLE render driver for a layout switch — it calls `requestRender()` on the no-VT path and `forceLayout()` inside the VT update callback. Callers (`setResponsive`, `#checkBreakpoint`, `#checkMultiBreakpoint`) must NOT add their own `requestRender()`: on the VT path it runs synchronously BEFORE the update callback, scheduling a render of the pre-switch state around the snapshot.
- INVARIANT (Sep 2026): a `gridConfig` rebuild DETACHES and RE-ATTACHES the same plugin instance. `detach()` strips `data-responsive*` but keeps `#isResponsive`, so `attach()` must (a) re-assert the attributes via `#syncLayoutAttributes()` — otherwise the grid sits in card mode with none of the card CSS until the next resize, and the width-guarded `#checkBreakpoint` sees no change to correct it — (b) drop `#measuredCardHeight`/`#measuredGroupRowHeight`, and (c) `requestRender()` when responsive, because the cards on screen were built under the old config.
- INVARIANT: the card-mode `height: auto !important` is scoped `:not(.group-row, .responsive-card)`. It exists so the DEFAULT stacked-cell card grows to fit; applying it to a custom `cardRenderer` row makes `cardRowHeight` unobservable. Matching rule in `#getCardHeight()`: a numeric `cardRowHeight` wins unless the MEASURED height exceeds it (overflow); only `auto` hands the decision to the measurement.
- INVARIANT: `#syncMotionDuration()` (from `attach()` and `#commitLayoutSwitch`) is the SOLE writer of `--tbw-responsive-duration`, publishing `0ms` when `#animation === false` or `!isAnimationEnabled` — how the CSS keyframe and the VT groups, which cannot read plugin config, get silenced. `#viewTransitionStarter()` returns `null` under the same condition, so no view transition (hence no UA `-ua-view-transition-fade-*`) runs at all. See build-css.md → "animation vars are INLINE" for why that gate was dead before Jul 2026.
